title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East  (Late Show) on 1970-05-15
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > ZA2 > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of the May 15 1970 Fillmore East shows – crystal‑clear audio and a legendary mix of acoustic, NRPS and electric sets.
ai_review.review: This SBD from the early/late Fillmore East marathon is praised for its studio‑like clarity with only occasional minor glitches.  The performance showcases an all‑time great acoustic set (Friend of the Devil, Long Black Limousine), superb New Riders interludes and electric highlights such as Dark Star, The Other One, Easy Wind and Good Lovin'.  Overall the show is hailed as one of the finest snapshots of the Dead’s 1970 peak.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 70 detailed reviews, >90 % rating 5‑stars and consistent praise for both performance and audio quality; only a few minor criticisms.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with bright highs, tight lows and good instrument separation; occasional brief drop‑outs or tape glitches noted but never detract from overall listening experience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two acoustic Dead sets bookend the New Riders of the Purple Sage interludes, followed by two electric Dead halves; the pacing moves from relaxed folk to high‑energy jams, creating a seamless narrative that captures the band’s 1970 transitional brilliance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone praised across acoustic and electric numbers; his pedal‑steel with NRPS described as “sweet sorghum syrup” and his vocals noted as heartfelt even when a lyric flub occurs.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass highlighted for its thunderous roll on The Other One and overall tight, driving foundation throughout the sets.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s banter, organ work (especially on Rub and Lovelight) and vocal grit are repeatedly called “on fire” and a major part of the show’s charm.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drum solo in the early electric set is noted as “extensive” and his percussion praised for adding swing to Dark Star.
